thread:
maria: FYI a customer in enterprise-tier opened a P0 — p99 latency jumped after yesterday's quantization profile push. They reported tail latencies ~1.1s from ~320ms. Attaching their repro logs (redacted) and timeline.

ajay: ack. which cluster / model variant?

maria: model: rwd-base-13b, serving tag: quant-profile-v2.3 (int8 preferred, fallback fp16). Cluster: inference-prod-3 (us-west-2). Deploy-bot shows rollout at 2024-09-08T21:12:04Z. Customer says the spike started ~10m after.

deploy-bot: rolled out quant-profile-v2.3 -> inference-prod-3 at 1716197524 (canary 10% -> 100%). :rocket:

leo: quick hypothesis: int8 kernel path increases per-token latency for certain seq lengths when kernel selection picks small-block GEMM (cache-unfriendly). Seen before with fp8 toggles too. Any sequence length distribution from their requests?

maria: customer supplied sample: most requests are short prompts (<=64 tokens) but they have occasional long-context requests up to 1024 tokens. They say p50 unchanged, p95 rose from 320ms -> 580ms, p99 to 1.1s.

ajay: reproduce steps I'm running locally against a canary VM. Reproducer:
```bash
# short prompt (64 tokens)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"rwd-base-13b","input":"lorem ipsum ...","max_tokens":64}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
I'll sweep toggles: --quant=int8, --quant=fp8, force-fp16.

leo: check calibration too. If calibration tables are stale or the per-channel scales are off, fallback paths might incur extra computing (padding, dequant/requant). Also check KV cache behavior — int8 KV cache may be slower if we convert per-step.

ajay: quick results: int8 path: p95 ~640ms p99 ~1.05s on canary; force fp16: p95 ~340ms p99 ~420ms. fp8 path similar to int8 in this run. So yes, quant path is the culprit.

maria: customer is on Dedicated but pinned to latest profile via team config. They want immediate mitigation.

sara: mitigation plan: 1) rollback quant-profile-v2.3 on inference-prod-3 ASAP for dedicated customers (pin back to v2.2). 2) add canary routing to send small fraction to quant path only when seq_len<=128. 3) create a hotfix to skip int8 kernels for small batches until perf tuned. Who can roll back?

ajay: I can push rollback. Rolling revert to v2.2 on inference-prod-3 now. I'll prefer rolling restart on a subset to avoid mass flaps.

deploy-bot: starting rollback: quant-profile-v2.2 -> inference-prod-3 (step 1/4) at 1716201420

ajay: done for canary nodes — observed tail drop: p99 back to ~430-480ms for canary. Proceeding to remaining nodes.

maria: I told customer we have rollback in progress and asked for confirmation if they still see high tail. Also requested a sample of their long-context requests for deeper profiling.

leo: follow-ups (post-mortem items):
- instrument kernel selection metrics (GEMM type, block-size, precision) at request-level so we can correlate quant-choice -> latency.
- add a calibration audit: when changing quant profiles, run a quick perf sweep over seq_len buckets [<=64, 65-256, 257-1024] and batch sizes [1,4,8] and fail rollout if any p95 regresses >20%.
- add an automatic fallback policy: if quant path p95 > baseline*1.3, route to fp16 automatically for that model/cluster.

maria: CHORE: i'm opening a support postmortem and tagging engineering. Also logging this as a Sev3 for now until the rollback fully stabilizes.

ajay: additional note — calibration step we used for v2.3 used a mostly long-context corpus (avg 512 tokens). That biased quant scales for larger tokens and appears to have degraded small-seq kernel efficiency. We should decouple calibration dataset from perf-sensitive seq buckets.

sara: good call. For immediate action items I'll: 1) monitor p95/p99 via console dashboards for next 2 hours, set alert threshold p99 > 600ms for this model on prod, 2) throttle new quant-profile rollouts until we have the perf sweep gating.

maria: thanks team. I'll share the customer confirmation when they reply. Leaving notes on the ticket: rollback done, root cause likely quant-profile calibration skew + kernel selection regressions. Will include repro steps and cli commands we used.

ajay: once things are stable i'll create a small harness (perf-sweep) and a PR to the rollout pipeline to run it automatically.

leo: and we'll add a metric for "quantization-fallback-rate" (how often we fall back to fp16 at runtime) — high rates indicate calibration trouble.

maria: customer just confirmed tail latencies returned to normal on their end :thumbsup:. Closing P0 to P1, will keep monitoring.

sara: nice. will follow up with a blameless postmortem doc and action owners. :tada:
